clue.text: Cowboy giving some of his money to a bounder

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, a slice of an American cowboy's cash
a kangaroo bounds, and roo is its short form

explanation.surface: A cowboy hands part of his wages to a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like the old word for a scoundrel, but here it is the jumping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an American term for a ranch hand, from Spanish vaquero.

clue.text: Read the future — frightening, empty

indicators.note: empty here means the word is emptied of its lone vowel A, left without it

parts.note: frightening means scary

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's prediction turns out both alarming and hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' removes the A from SCARY, leaving the consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the future in a crystal ball or mirror is the old verb for divining.

clue.text: Intended fund to have name excised

indicators.note: excised means cut out, so the letter for name is taken away from the word for fund

parts.note: to fund something is to finance it

explanation.surface: A planned fund is set to have someone's name struck off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' reads as an adjective meaning planned, but it is the noun for one's husband-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's intended is the person they are engaged to marry, here the man.

clue.text: Vacuum-maker finds first-rate Bottom cradling head of Puck

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: cradling means holding within, so the word for bottom wraps round the letter

parts.note: the bottom is the rump

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Midsummer Night's Dream scene: the excellent weaver Bottom cradles the head of the sprite Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom and Puck are characters in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, which makes 'Bottom' look like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump that sucks air out of a vessel produces a vacuum inside it.

clue.text: Film the French keeping distance from film

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the word for film holds the measure

parts.note: a pic is informal for a film or picture
an ell is an old measure of length
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Something about a French movie kept at arm's length from cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Film' is a thin skin or membrane, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thin skin or membrane, such as a layer forming on a liquid's surface.

clue.text: Bullied ex-PM husbanding rhythm and energy

indicators.note: husbanding means carefully keeping, so the former leader's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Gordon Brown was a British prime minister
a beat is a rhythm
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A former prime minister bullies people while conserving his rhythm and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown, UK prime minister 2007-10, had a reputation for a fierce temper, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intimidated by harsh words and stern looks has been bullied.

clue.text: Fee for one being looked after

definitions.meaning: a price asked for a service
a person in someone's care, such as a ward

explanation.surface: A cost of care for a dependant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a price levied and a person entrusted to another's care.

clue.text: South African (half-cut) visits Sark etc, receiving cheers (also half-cut) for vegetable

indicators.note: half-cut means drunk, but here the word is cut in half and loses its second part

parts.note: a Zulu is one of a South African people

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the islands' letters hold the other piece

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

indicators.note: also half-cut means this toast too is cut in half, losing one repeat

parts.note: chin-chin is an old drinking toast, like cheers

explanation.surface: A tipsy South African visits the Channel Islands, where drunken toasts are drunk over a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which fits the toasts, but it means halving the words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American and Italian name for the courgette, a green summer squash.

clue.text: Planet-beater, head to tail

indicators.note: head to tail means the first letter is moved round to the end

parts.note: the heart is the organ that beats

explanation.surface: Something that beats the world, moving from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Our world is the third planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Ring animal back, alright?

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: back means the animal's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether calling an animal back is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an informal assent meaning all right or acceptable.

clue.text: Plant tool for gardener getting quiet leg-over

indicators.note: over means the whole string of pieces is turned backwards

parts.note: a trowel is a small gardening tool
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A gardener with a tool gets a quiet bit of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg-over' is British slang for sexual intercourse; here it splits into 'leg' and the reversal signal 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common yellow-flowered weed of the daisy family, once used for sore breasts.

clue.text: Born villain's dialect?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that an accent is not quite a dialect

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born in biographies
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A natural-born scoundrel's way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one, so loosely a dialect.

clue.text: Cutting back on concerts in system that favours fat cats?

definitions.note: the question mark admits this is a jaundiced view of short-term freelance work

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the second piece sits after the first

parts.note: a gig is a pop concert
economy is cutting back on spending

explanation.surface: Reducing spending on concerts in a system that rewards rich bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting back on concerts' reads as one phrase, but it is the saving placed after the word for concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-term freelance work is said to enrich platform owners while workers lack security.

clue.text: Having coat on boat, catching river fish

indicators.note: on means the coat comes before the boat

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the boat's word takes in the letter

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat, a barge

explanation.surface: A coated angler on a boat catches a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A keel is also an old word for a barge, as in the song 'The Keel Row'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a striped sea fish of the tuna family, common in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Trick and joke, reportedly, with clog

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for joke is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A prank and a joke involving a wooden shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clog' looks like the noun for a shoe but is the verb meaning block.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog a pipe or a road is to block it up so nothing flows.

clue.text: Homeless animal's style of singing captivates carrier

indicators.note: captivates suggests holding captive, so the singing style surrounds the carrier

parts.note: scat is jazz singing with nonsense syllables
a tray carries food and drinks

explanation.surface: A homeless creature's singing charms a postman or other carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic feline without an owner roams the streets.

clue.text: Fabric persona non grata's getting time after time

indicators.note: after means the outcast's word follows the other time

parts.note: T again stands for time

indicators.note: getting means taking in, so the banished person's word receives a letter

parts.note: someone unwelcome may be an exile, banished from home

explanation.surface: An unwelcome diplomat's material is put in place time after time.
explanation.definitionFit: Woven cloth is a fabric, the word coming from Latin for woven.

clue.text: Letter to innkeeper

definitions.meaning: one who lets out property, an owner taking rent
the person running a pub or inn

explanation.surface: A note sent to a publican.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who lets property and a publican.

clue.text: Unhygienic person strangely able to get cigarette out

indicators.note: out means the cigarette's word sits outside the shuffled letters

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of the next word appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A grubby person oddly manages to pull out a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' makes LEABA from ABLE, which the cigarette's three letters go round.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruffy, dirty person is insultingly called this, as if crawling with insects.

clue.text: Ghostly second muscle wanting nothing

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is taken out of the muscle

parts.note: a pectoral is a chest muscle
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A spooky moment as a muscle fails to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phantom-like, belonging to a spirit or apparition, is ghostly.

clue.text: Mate's essay is far from great

parts.note: a pal is a mate
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A friend's school essay is a poor effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a school composition but is the old sense of an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A meagre, trifling amount is far from great.

clue.text: Preparing to play with erotic writer, pull out

indicators.note: out means the pull's word goes on the outside

parts.note: to tug is to pull
Anais Nin wrote famous erotica

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a game with a racy author, then withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians adjust the pitch of their instruments before a performance.

clue.text: Rows about origin of ginger cats

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rows go round the letter

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Arguments break out about where ginger cats come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels, but it means rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: These striped big felines are members of the cat family.

clue.text: Unknown pianist hugging unknown tree

parts.note: in algebra Y is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: hugging means enclosing, so the pianist's name wraps round the letter

parts.note: Lang Lang is a Chinese concert pianist
Y again stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: An obscure pianist embraces a mysterious tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Asian tropical tree whose fragrant flowers yield a perfume oil.

clue.text: Part — of backward Time Lord?

indicators.note: backward says the hidden letters are read backwards
of here means taken out of, so the letters are drawn from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part played by Doctor Who, a Time Lord, going back in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden word no indicator; 'of' signals letters taken out of 'Time Lord'. A Time Lord is Doctor Who's alien race.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's part in a play or film is the character they portray.

clue.text: Party's not initially serious

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: grave means serious

explanation.surface: A party that isn't solemn at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild all-night dance party with electronic music is called this.

clue.text: Dance and drink to sailor's return

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: return means the sailor's letters come back in reverse

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home to dancing and drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Cuban ballroom dance with hip movements.

clue.text: RADA 5, surprisingly, aboard floating zoo with one of its occupants?

indicators.note: aboard means the shuffled letters are put on the vessel, inside it

parts.note: Noah's Ark carried animals in pairs, a floating zoo

indicators.note: surprisingly means these letters appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: RADA is taken as written and 5 is V in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Drama school graduates are surprisingly put aboard Noah's Ark with the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art; '5' is not the cross-reference it seems but the Roman V. 'surprisingly' turns RADA plus V into ARDVA.
explanation.definitionFit: An African burrowing mammal would be one of the beasts on Noah's vessel, first alphabetically.
